audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive late-game interaction was absent: Highlander makes Master Yi IMMUNE TO ALL SLOWING EFFECTS. Bramble Smash's slow and Sapling Toss's slow are blanked while it is up — but a root is not a slow, so Twisted Advance and Nature's Grasp still hold him. The page told you to 'peel him off your carries' without saying which half of your kit stops working.
audit.why: Riot R text: 'temporarily increasing his Move Speed and Attack Speed as well as making him immune to all slowing effects.' That is the difference between a peel that works and one that does nothing, and it is exactly the kind of thing a player finds out the hard way in a teamfight.

This is one of the 92 inherited structural gaps and needs a deliberate scaffold pass, not an audit edit.

The 44.76% / 6-of-7-stages contradiction is the sharpest data conflict in my slice: the page tells the reader they dominate every stage of a lane they lose more often than they win. Two readings are possible — (a) the chart is right and Maokai's losses come from Master Yi's mid-game jungle-style snowball off other lanes rather than from the lane itself, or (b) the chart is inherited boilerplate and several rows should be Skill. I could not distinguish these from the kits and did not guess. Flagged in questionsForUser.

DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: Meditate carries a derived 'channel: interruptible — any CC cancels it' flag, which would make 'W-root cancels his Meditate' a fantastic line. Riot's own description says only that it restores Health, reduces damage taken, and pauses Wuju Style and Highlander durations — it never says the channel breaks on CC. Under the brief's needsResearch rule that is UNKNOWN, not 'yes', so it stays off the page. It is a strong candidate for the research queue.

Champion-level kit-flag defect (eighth time): Maokai's Q carries a 'grounding' flag Riot's description does not support. Not asserted — note it would have been decisive here against Alpha Strike.
